sim2real logo · round 3 · 20 variants, each in context

2026-10-28 · from his round-2 favourites: the dissolve into pixels, the breakout, viewfinder and loupe, and s2r text that can't be read as c2r

Recommend R3-01 Dissolve Trail, then R3-02 Loupe II and R3-03 Viewfinder Brackets.

Simplified, as asked: one chunky 8-tooth gear, pixels as big blocks (about five across the gear), flat steel with a thick rim, thick frames. Every variant has a one-colour silhouette at 16, 24 and 32 px, and is shown in light and dark where it will live: a website header, a browser tab at 16 and 32 px, a desktop icon and dock, and Clank's sidebar next to Robot Parts and BAM Robotics.

Pick any (★), comment, then Copy my picks and paste the text into chat. Round 1's toolbar icon stays Clank's default until a logo is picked and simplified.

"something like turning pixeled and then kinda like going off into pixelated land ... you kinda like leave out certain of the pixels ... I really like the break out one ... similar idea with the view finder and loupe: That one is very strong" · "their level of detail is a bit too high. please simplify if possible so they look good kinda from a silhouette, and smaller. Make sure to show a dark and light mode for the icons." Zach, 2026-10-28

#1 · score 94

R3-01 Dissolve Trail

favicon at 16 and 32 px
silhouette at 16, 24, 32 px

His sentence drawn: the gear 'turning pixeled and then going off into pixelated land', its right side breaking into blocks, one in four left out, the rest trailing away. As a silhouette it is still a gear and a line of squares at 16 px.

#2 · score 91

R3-02 Loupe II

favicon at 16 and 32 px
silhouette at 16, 24, 32 px

The loupe he called very strong, simplified: a heavy ring over the teeth and a few big blocks inside it. Magnifier plus gear survives in a browser tab and in the one-colour test.

#3 · score 91

R3-03 Viewfinder Brackets

favicon at 16 and 32 px
silhouette at 16, 24, 32 px

The viewfinder at its simplest: four thick corner brackets, blocks inside, steel outside, no device. The shortest path to a 24 px icon.

The c2r check

"if you have s2r c2r like visually they start to look very very similar." A plain s2r and a plain c2r really are almost the same picture at favicon size; every round-3 mark carries the dissolving gear, so none of them is.

16 px32 px64 pxdifferent from plain c2r at 16 px
plain c2rthe referencewhat a text-only cad2robot mark would look like
plain s2r3.4%the problem: one letter's bowl apart
cad2robot today—its real favicon: an orange tile with an arm, so no clash with any of these today
R3-19 s2r Dissolve11.6%text-led
R3-15 Gear Badge18.4%text-led
R3-16 Tile Monogram44.0%text-led
R3-01 Dissolve Trail14.2%the recommendation

Measured, not judged: each mark and a plain "c2r" in the same face, both rendered at 16 × 16 in greyscale; the mean absolute difference per pixel. A plain s2r is 3.4% away from c2r. The three text-led marks are 3.4× to 13× further away, and the least distinct of all 20 (s2r Dissolve) is still 11.6%.

Notes

How they are built

  • A small kit in brand/logos/round3/marks3.py: one 8-tooth gear with a big bore, blocks on a grid about five across it, flat steel (one soft gradient, a thick rim, a soft shadow), thick frames. No lathe rings, bevels, screen grids or glare: those were the detail that turned to mush at 16 px.
  • Every mark has a one-colour mode (mono): steel and blocks in ink, frames as thick outlines, knock-outs in the background colour. That is both the silhouette test and the start of the 24 px icon.
  • The dissolve: each grid cell of the gear stays steel or becomes a block; some blocks are left out, the rest drift off and shrink. R3-01's trail is placed by hand, since a seeded scatter of so few blocks left too little to read.
  • Rendered headlessly at 240, 48, 32, 24 and 16 px, light and dark, and looked at. Fixed after looking: holes punched in the metal (Chrome merges a clipPath's children, so the keep-region is a mask), the hub vanishing where a gear broke up, viewfinder brackets merging with a dark fill into one black square, too few blocks in the trail.

Context mocks

  • Clank's sidebar copies the three styles in clank-workbench/reports/media/clank-sidebar-styles-2026-10-26.html (Obsidian rail, Figma rail, Shopify list; light #F6F6F6, dark #262626), with Robot Parts' and BAM Robotics' real icons. Clank itself was only read.
  • The tab strip uses the real 16 and 32 px rasters; its neighbours are robotparts.dev and cad2robot.com's real favicons.
  • Palette: BAM Grid Purist, ink #0E100E, paper #FBFBF8, BAM Green #2F6F4F, lit #35DE95 on dark.

Files

  • brand/logos/round3/NN-slug.svg, -dark.svg, -lockup.svg, -lockup-dark.svg; preview/NN-slug-16.png, -32.png (and dark).
  • Rebuild: render3.py --previews, then build3.py (commands in brand/logos/round3/README.md).
